correctness.rationale: The claim follows from the odd-part definition by exact prefix-sum recurrences. The proof derives S(2^m-1)=2^(m-1)-1 and S(L_m)=floor(L_m/2)-floor((m-1)/2), then computes an explicit length-L_m factor whose excess over the length-L_m prefix is exactly m-1. For any fixed c, choosing m>=c+2 makes that factor beat the length-L_m prefix of 1^c p. The bundled verifier independently checks every algebraic identity on a broad finite range, but the quantified conclusion is supplied by induction rather than finite extrapolation.

value.rationale: Finite prepend-normalizability is a named structural question in the anchor paper: it separates Sturmian and Thue-Morse examples from Champernowne. The same paper treats paperfolding in detail but leaves that qualitative behavior unstated. The result places this classical automatic word decisively on the non-normalizable side and supplies a reusable logarithmic obstruction family rather than an isolated finite counterexample.
